name: Gold real price mean reversion (the golden dilemma)

how_it_works.simple: Divide the gold price by the cost of living. When that ratio is far above its long-run average, expect poor gold returns over the next decade; when it is far below, expect good ones.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a house that costs ten times local incomes: it can stay expensive for years, but buyers who pay that much have usually done badly over the next decade.
how_it_works.precise: The real price of gold is the nominal price divided by the US CPI. Erb and Harvey show that since US gold futures began trading, a high real price has been followed by low subsequent 10-year real gold returns, as with stock market valuation ratios. A trading version holds less gold, or none, when the real price is in the top part of its history.

rule: Our simple version, for testing: each month, compute gold / CPI and its percentile against all earlier months since 1975. Hold gold when the ratio is below its historical median, hold cash when above. This rule is ours, not the paper's.
data_needed: World Bank Pink Sheet monthly gold, silver and platinum prices (free, DAT-0035)
US CPI (FRED CPIAUCSL, free; not yet in our catalog)
economic_rationale: Gold has no cash flow, so over long horizons its price should track the general price level; deviations from that are eventually corrected as mine supply, recycling and jewellery demand respond to price.
why_it_might_fail: The authors call the relation a 'known unknown': there are only a few independent decades since 1975, so the chart rests on one big cycle (1980 high, 2001 low, 2011 high). Central bank buying, which the paper flags as the other side of the dilemma, can keep the real price high for a long time.

reported_results.source: Erb and Harvey (2013), Financial Analysts Journal, Figure 5 and text
reported_results.notes: Since gold futures began trading, gold / CPI averaged about 3.2, with a low of 1.46 (March 2001) and a high of 8.73 (January 1980); it was 7.3 at the end of March 2012. If the Figure 5 relation were stable, that level would imply a future 10-year real return of about -10% a year, which the authors stress is not a reliable forecast. A regression chart, not a trading backtest.

post_publication_evidence: Not checked by us yet. The paper's March 2012 reading gives a clean forecast to check against the World Bank's monthly gold price for 2012 to 2022.

relevance.reason: Gold is the metal retail investors buy most, and 'gold is cheap or expensive' is a common pitch; this is the most cited honest test of it, and free monthly data covers it.

research.notes: Testable with the World Bank's monthly gold price and FRED CPI; neither is wired into the engine yet. Added in Amanda's metals batch on 2026-10-25.
